standard.title: Add and subtract fractions
standard.description: Solve problems involving addition and subtraction of fractions with the same or related denominators, using different strategies
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can compare and order fractions with the same and related denominators and generate equivalent fractions (AC9M4N06, AC9M5N03). They have not yet added or subtracted fractions requiring denominator conversion.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students solve problems involving addition and subtraction of fractions with the same or related denominators using different strategies.

nodes.label: Adding and subtracting with same denominators
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can add and subtract fractions with the same denominator, explaining the procedure in terms of unit fractions.
nodes.minimum_width: Add and subtract fractions with the same denominator; express the result as a simplified fraction or mixed numeral where applicable.
nodes.typical_width: Solve a range of same-denominator problems including results greater than 1; connect to number line jumps; explain why denominators do not change.
wider: Use measurement contexts (e.g. adding lengths in fractions of a metre)
Model with fraction bars or area models

response_modes.reason: Students commonly add denominators as well as numerators. Targeted practice with the 'add numerators, keep denominator' principle needs to precede related-denominator work.

nodes.hinge_reason: The 'add denominators' error propagates directly into Node 2 — students who have not consolidated same-denominator operations apply the same error after conversion, producing systematically wrong results.
success_criteria: Student explains why the denominator remains unchanged

nodes.label: Adding and subtracting with related denominators
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can add and subtract fractions with related denominators by converting to a common denominator.
nodes.minimum_width: Convert one fraction to match the other's denominator and then add or subtract; verify the result.
nodes.typical_width: Solve problems involving fractions with related denominators; choose the most efficient equivalent form; express answers in simplest form.
wider: Use cooking or construction problem contexts requiring fraction addition
Solve multi-step problems combining same and related denominator fractions

response_modes.reason: The conversion step requires an explicit sequence: identify related denominators → find conversion factor → convert → operate → simplify. Without scaffolding, students conflate or skip steps.
Related denominators vary — some pairs are obvious (halves/quarters), some less so (thirds/sixths, fifths/tenths). Varied pairs prevent students from learning a single pattern.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Real-world contexts (cooking, construction) give advancing students purposeful multi-step problems.
nodes.hinge_reason: The conversion-then-operate sequence is the prerequisite for Node 3 — students who skip or conflate steps cannot reliably tackle multi-step problems where both same and related denominator operations occur.
success_criteria: Student correctly converts to a common denominator and completes the operation
Student expresses the result in simplest form

nodes.label: Multi-step fraction problems
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can solve multi-step problems involving both addition and subtraction of fractions with same or related denominators.
nodes.minimum_width: Solve a problem requiring both addition and subtraction of fractions with related denominators; show each step.
nodes.typical_width: Apply addition and subtraction of fractions in multi-step practical problems; connect to measurement and cooking contexts; check answers using equivalent forms.
wider: Design and solve original fraction problems for peers involving multiple operations
Connect fraction operations to percentage equivalents: adding 1/4 and 3/10 via common denominator vs via percentages

response_modes.reason: Multi-step fraction problems require same-denominator operations, related-denominator conversion and simplification to work together in sequence — the integration of all prior fraction reasoning.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Multi-step problems and fraction–percentage connections give advancing students rich, creative territory.
success_criteria: Student solves a multi-step fraction problem showing each operation
Student expresses the final answer in simplest form
